title: This Fish Hitchhikes on Sharks Using a Fin Turned Into a Sucker

scenes.text: This fish rides sharks, and it hardly spends any energy holding on.
It's a remora. On top of its head, its dorsal fin has flattened into an oval suction pad.
Inside the pad, rows of plates carry tiny tooth-like spikes that grip the skin.
Researchers think the grip is passive, and the shark's own swimming drag may make it stronger.
It even holds best on mako sharks. The spike spacing matches the shark's scales.
To let go, it lowers the plates with tiny muscles. A hitchhiker with a built-in release.
